Staffordshire' with a crown (Victorian Porcelain, Longton), so the researcher's 'Wileman-style' label is wrong. lots.guide_summary: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking survive. All five researcher entries were retail asks (AUD 360 to 2,625 at assumed rates). Every page (georgianantiques.net, napoleonexhibit.com, patternbyetsy.com, 1stdibs.com) was blocked and none could be re-seen, so all were dropped. The two 1stdibs URLs are category pages, not individual listings. Even unverified, dealer asks for boxes in good order would run far above what a box with missing quills fetches at auction.

lots.confidence_reason: The quill box identification is clear from the photos, but it is damaged and there is no verified evidence of any kind.

lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged photo 4: the quill box has clear quill loss on the front and side panels, with the bare wood backing showing in several sections. The lid panels look mostly complete, and the bone studs and frame are intact. Photo 2: the fish set shows 6 forks and 5 knives (one knife looks short or missing), with carved MOP handles, plated engraved blades with some wear, and a brass plaque. Photo 3: the case lid has a long crack across the top. No hallmarks are visible on anything, so treat it all as plated.
lots.condition: The quill box has significant quill loss on the sides. The fish case lid is cracked and the blades show plating wear. The loose knives have yellowed handles, probably bone or celluloid, with ivory unconfirmed.
lots.question_for_armitage: How big is the quill box, and does it have an interior fitting or mirror? Can you confirm how many quills are missing on each side? Is the fish set 5 or 6 knives? Are the loose knife handles bone, celluloid or ivory?
